gap: No result ChatGPT got states the EG4 FlexBOSS21's surge rating beyond half a second (18,000 W for 1 s, 15,000 W for 6 min, 13,200 W for 12 min), so its '24 kW' surge cannot be set beside the Sol-Ark 15K's 24,000 VA held for 10 s.
standout_why: I read three of the cited pages: liveoffthegrid.com/specs/inverters, ecosolarkits.com eg4-vs-sol-ark and ecosolarkits.com split-phase-inverter-explained. The cited Sol-Ark one-pager returned 404. liveoffthegrid lists one surge figure per model with no time window and no FlexBOSS21 row. The eg4-vs-sol-ark page warns that surge windows differ (0.5 s, 10 s, 10 min) but gives the FlexBOSS21 surge as 'see spec sheet'. The explainer gives 24 kW (0.5 s) for the FlexBOSS21 and 16,000 VA (10 s) for the Sol-Ark 12K, with no 15K row. None of them gives the FlexBOSS21's 1 s, 6 min or 12 min ratings, so none puts the two inverters on the same time window. I did not open the uncited gearranking, solargearscout, solarpanelx, portlandia or apesolar pages, so one of them may hold the curve.
decides: This confirms the order ChatGPT gave and puts a number on the Sol-Ark 15K's premium. Both inverters are 12 kW on battery alone. Read over the same window, though, the Sol-Ark holds 24,000 VA for 10 s while the FlexBOSS21 drops to 18,000 W by 1 s. A shopper starting large motors (well pump, central AC) off-grid should lean Sol-Ark 15K. For a grid-tied home with ordinary loads the FlexBOSS21 stays the value pick: 12 kW on battery, 16 kW with PV, at $3,599.99 against $5,650. Over about 10 minutes the FlexBOSS21 (15 kW at 6 min, 13.2 kW at 12 min) and the EG4 18kPV (13.5 kW for 10 min without PV) come out close.

findings.value: 12,000 W (12,000 VA) without PV; 16,000 W at 240 V or 13,800 W at 208 V with PV
findings.note: Maker's US product page. It says 12 kW 'to loads/battery without PV' and 16 kW 'to grid or load with PV/battery'. Max continuous AC current is listed as 50 A. The page gives no surge or per-leg figure.

findings.label: Grid bypass (pass-through) current
findings.note: The page says it can 'feed-through 90 Amps of utility power from the grid'. This is grid current passed through to loads, not inverter output. Read as power, 90 A × 240 V = 21.6 kW of grid power, not backup power.

findings.label: Surge curve (peak power vs duration)
findings.value: 24,000 W for 0.5 s; 18,000 W for 1 s; 15,000 W for 6 min; 13,200 W for 12 min
findings.note: Retailer spec table under 'Inverter Specifications', linked to an EG4 spec sheet PDF that I could not read as text. Neither the EG4 product page nor the EG4 spec sheet PDF (eg4electronics.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/EG4-FlexBoss21-Spec-Sheet.pdf) gave readable text, so this is a retailer copy of the maker figure, not checked against the maker. The same table lists 'Max. Output Current: 66.7A' (16 kW ÷ 240 V) and 'Max. AC Current: 50A @ 240V'. My inference: by linear interpolation between the 6 min and 12 min points the rating is about 14.1 kW at 10 min.
